newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major says no need for EU panic over beef.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major says no need for EU panic over beef.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major said on Thursday new scientific evidence would not justify the European Union changing its stance on lifting the ban on British beef exports.
He was speaking after news that British scientists had found evidence that people can get a new human form of mad cow disease from eating contaminated beef.
Major said Britain had been taking measures to stamp out Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy for years, and had recently enlarged on those measures.
"There is no need for any more action, and because the action has been taken there is no need for the European Union to panic and change its views," Major said in an interview with BBC television.
"There is no fresh public health concern. People can eat beef as safely today as they could yesterday and I think it is perfectly safe," he said.

Major won an agreement from his EU partners at a summit meeting in Florence this summer for a gradual lifting of the beef export ban. However, little has happened since then to enable exports to resume. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
